carl: heads-up — trying nsys capture inside a k8s pod without privileged mode, kernel timeline is almost empty. suspect nsight can't attach to device. anyone seen this?
kevin: yup. nvidia-container-toolkit blocks some ioctls by default. we usually either run the pod privileged or bind /dev/nvidia* into the container. not great for prod though.
mia: repro steps i used:
```
kubectl run profiler --image=redwood/inference-dev:staging --restart=Never --overrides='{"spec":{...}}'
nsys profile --output=trace.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --capture-range=cpu
```
nsys starts but trace.nsys has no kernel timeline, only memcpy and runtime stuff.
josh: did you check file permissions on /tmp/.nv? last time a stale root-owned socket made nsight bail. also check nvidia-container-toolkit log inside the pod.
carl: checked — /tmp/.nv and /var/lib/nvidia were root:root and mode 700. i tried `chown 1000:1000 /tmp/.nv` and got a partial timeline but still missing cuBLAS kernels.
kevin: partial timeline makes me think kernel selection fallback happened — runtime probably switched to a fallback GEMM kernel because we hit an ISA/kernel mismatch in the optimized kernels. that sometimes shows as a lot of small pointwise kernels instead of a big gemm.
mia: interesting — we saw a perf regression after the runtime change at commit abc123. mapping shows more small-kernel launches around attention and ffwrd.
josh: can you paste the nvprof-like snippet? small example from a trace:
```
# simplified timeline
MemcpyHtoD 2ms
launch conv_small_kernel 0.8ms
launch gemm_fallback_64x64 5.2ms
...
```
kevin: that `gemm_fallback_64x64` is the giveaway. kernel selector probably switched because it couldn't load the fast kernel (missing cuBLAS or kernel binary failed to JIT). in containerized setups the JIT temp dir or executable permission problems cause that.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: staging inferred-runtime updated: runtime/optimizer @ abc123 -> def456 :rocket:
carl: i tried running the same workload on the node host (nsys from host but targeting the container pidns) and timeline is complete with big gemm kernels. so it's definitely container permission/attach related.
mia: potential repro checklist for eng-runtime to triage:
- run pod unprivileged (current)
- run pod with `--device=/dev/nvidia0` and `volumeMount` for /tmp
- run pod privileged as a control
- capture `dmesg` and toolkit logs
- collect nsys + perfetto trace from host and container
kevin: quick workaround: mount `/tmp` as emptyDir with hostUID fix and chown to container user at init. also add device mounts: `volumeMounts: - hostPath: /dev/nvidia0`.
josh: long-term fix: update nvidia-container-toolkit config to allow required device cgroup ops and add a startup hook to ensure `/tmp/.nv` owned by runtime user. also need to repro kernel-selection failure in CI with perf traces so we catch regressions.
carl: i can attach a minimal perf repro tomorrow and capture both host and in-container nsys. i'll stash the traces in the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/1858203142/
mia: please include the `env` diff we used (notably `CUDA_CACHE_PATH`, `CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_SO_LOAD`, `LD_PRELOAD`) — those influence kernel JIT behavior.
kevin: also run `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublas.so | grep kernel` to see available kernels in the binary
josh: note — if we hit fallback during sequence length 2048 it costs ~30% more token latency. we need a job to detect sudden shifts in kernel mix in Optimize.
mia: agree. for now i'll add a quick alert in Console: if gemm_fallback count / total > 0.1 fire regression alert.
carl: thanks. i'll upload traces and ping the thread when done. tagging @kevin to own the triage.
kevin: on it. will try repro with toolkit v1.11 and v1.13 to narrow the change. :mag:
